question.problem:
Which of the following are orthogonal projection matrices?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{10} & -\frac{3}{10} \\ -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $Q$ is an orthogonal projection matrix if and only if ${Q}^{2}=Q$ and ${Q}^{T}=Q.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have
${A}^{T}=A$
but 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 \\ -5 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne A.\end{aligned}
$$

- $B$ is an orthogonal projection matrix. Indeed,
${B}^{T}=B$
and

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{2} & =B\cdot B \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{10} & -\frac{3}{10} \\ -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{10} & -\frac{3}{10} \\ -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{100}[\begin{aligned}9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{100}[\begin{aligned}90 & -30 \\ -30 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{10} & -\frac{3}{10} \\ -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

- $C$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have
${C}^{T}=C$
but 

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{2} & =C\cdot C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13 & 4 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only."
